text_simplified: This text discusses the rights of children upon their parents in Islam, mentioning Prophetic hadiths that urge raising children with justice and ihsan (excellence). It also highlights the importance of teaching them prayer and instilling religious values in their hearts from a young age. It emphasizes that the tarbiyah (upbringing) of children is a great responsibility for which parents will be questioned on the Day of Judgment.

review_defects.arabic: حقوق الأبناء على الآباء في الإسلام
review_defects.english: The Rights of Children upon Their Parents in Islam
review_defects.why: The Arabic 'الآباء' means 'fathers', but the English translates it as 'Parents', which includes mothers. This broadens the meaning.

review_defects.english: instilling religious values in their hearts
review_defects.why: The Arabic 'نفوسهم' means 'their souls/self', not specifically 'hearts' (قلوبهم). The English substitutes 'hearts', which is a different concept.
